ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a five-minute time limit per person has been established. Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibits the Council from discussing or taking action on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council comments; however, items which are not on the agenda will be limited to Council reports, announcements, requests for clarification or factual information, or placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.

7.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. There may be separate discussions of these items prior to the time the Council votes on the motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Agenda at the request of any Council Member or staff.

8.
DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF REFINANCING OPTIONS AVAILABLE TO THE CITY TO REDUCE CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS) UNFUNDED ACCRUED LIABILITY (UAL) PENSION COSTS
Presented by Susan Kamada, Administrative Services Director and Kosmont Transaction Services
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Representatives from Kosmont Transactions Services (KTS) will be making a more detailed follow up presentation to the City Council regarding the options for refinancing the City’s CalPERS unfunded accrued liability (UAL) with bonds. Following the presentation (which will review the details of the various options available to the City Council), staff will be looking for direction regarding whether the City should proceed with issuance of lease revenue bonds or pension obligation bonds through court validation.
Based on the estimates provided by KTS, the recommendation of the Finance Committee is to direct staff and KTS to proceed with preparation of the instruments necessary to refinance the UAL through the issuance of Lease Revenue Bonds, return to the City Council with discussion regarding City assets available as collateral for the bonds.
Item No 8
9.
DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION ADOPTING THE LOMITA TREE SPECIES PALATE AND CONSIDERATION OF AMENDMENTS TO EXISTING POLICIES
Presented by Carla Dillon, Public Works Director
RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Adopt resolution 2021-30 adopting the Lomita Tree Species Palate; and 2) Discuss existing policies listed in the Lomita Municipal Code related to tree planting, maintenance, removal, and replacement and provide general policy direction for any desired amendments to those policies; and 3) Establish a goal of planting 105% of trees removed for the next five years.
RESOLUTION NO. 2021- 30 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING THE 2021 TREE SPECIES PALATE AND FINDING THE SAME EXEMPT FROM CEQA
